findings.quote: We have identified significant weaknesses in relation to: • the Authority's Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) deficit • the oversight of the Authority's housing stock and finances

findings.paper_title: West Northants Council External Audit Results Report 2024-25 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Land and building valuations potentially overstated by £16.259m due to unresolved floor area errors from prior year
findings.detail: The 2023/24 audit identified three assets (value £33.67m) where floor areas used in valuations did not match floor plans held by the council. Revaluations decreased valuation by £6.358m (18.9% reduction). This error has been extrapolated across the whole land and building population valued using direct replacement cost method, suggesting potential overstatement of £16.259m. The issue remains unresolved for 2024/25.
findings.matters: Overstated property valuations directly inflate the asset base and net worth reported to lenders, potentially masking true financial distress. An 18.9% correction rate signals systematic measurement failure.
findings.figures: Three assets at £33.67m, adjustment of £6.358m (18.9%), extrapolated potential overstatement £16.259m
findings.quote: Our testing identified three assets (value £33.67m) where the floor areas used in the valuations did not match the floor plans held by the Council... We have extrapolated this error across the whole land and building population where they have been valued using direct replacement cost (DRC) method and the balance could be overstated by £16.259m.

findings.paper_title: West Northants Council External Audit Results Report 2024-25 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Audit opinion will be disclaimed; unable to conclude on opening balances, land valuations, debtors and creditors
findings.detail: The auditors cannot issue an unmodified opinion due to limitations imposed by prior-year backstop legislation. They lack assurance on opening balances for 2024/25 and will qualify their opinion on property, plant & equipment (revaluation issues), short-term creditors (material unidentified balance from prior year), and short-term debtors. This means the auditors have not formed an opinion on whether the financial statements give a true and fair view.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion signals that a lender cannot rely on the financial statements to assess the council's true financial position, and creditor classification issues directly affect the balance sheet reliability.
findings.figures: Opening balances unverified; prior-year land and building valuation floor area errors affect current year
findings.quote: Our anticipated financial statements audit report opinion will be disclaimed.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26
findings.headline: National Insurance increases driving structural cost pressures across social care workforce and providers
findings.detail: The Government's National Insurance increase (introduced late 2024) has created additional costs for care providers. Adults social care is experiencing £1.8m of inflationary uplifts above budgeted levels, partly driven by 6.7% National Living Wage increase. Children's trust carries £0.7m of overspend share from agreed pay award and employer NI changes effective April 2025.
findings.matters: These are structural cost increases imposed by national policy changes outside the council's control, but they're pushing large demand-led budgets deeper into deficit. They signal continued cost pressure for 2026-27 onwards.
findings.figures: £1.8m adult care inflationary uplift, 6.7% National Living Wage, £0.7m children's trust NI share
findings.quote: These were introduced late last year by national government and caused additional workforce costs, especially in the social care sector.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26
findings.headline: General contingency (£11.4m) nearly exhausted at mid-year, leaving minimal buffer for identified live risks
findings.detail: The council set aside £11.4m in general budget contingency to absorb in-year risks. At Period 4, this reserve is nearly fully deployed just to bring the forecast position from much worse to £9.6m overspend. This leaves minimal headroom. The council explicitly identifies risks that 'could potentially worsen between now and year end' within Adult Social Care, Children's Social Care, Home to School Transport, and Temporary Accommodation.
findings.matters: Once contingency is depleted, there is no financial buffer for the live risks the council has already identified. Further deterioration in demand-led services will flow directly to reserves or borrowing.
findings.figures: £11.4m contingency consumed, £9.6m forecast overspend (2.2% of net budget)
findings.quote: The forecast outturn position for 2025-26 is an overspend of £9.6m after the use of £11.4m of general budget contingencies, which were set aside in the budget for risks that may crystalise in the current financial year.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26
findings.headline: £6.6m of £24.6m savings target at risk: £1.0m red (unlikely to deliver) and £5.6m amber-flagged
findings.detail: Of £24.6m budgeted savings, only £7.0m (28%) confirmed delivered at mid-year. £11.1m (45%) on track. However, £5.6m (23%) is amber-flagged with delivery risks and £1.0m (4%) is red-flagged as unlikely to be delivered. The key failure is £0.3m expected from developer charges (linear rates) now delayed to November 2025, creating an immediate savings shortfall.
findings.matters: Savings shortfalls fall directly to the bottom line. The council is already £9.6m in overspend after using contingencies. Any savings slippage will either worsen the outturn or force further reserve draws.
findings.figures: £24.6m total requirement, £1.0m red, £5.6m amber, £0.3m linear rates delay
findings.quote: Following review of the Council's budgeted savings proposals. £1.0m has been assessed as red and therefore unlikely to be delivered.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26
findings.headline: Children's social care placements described as 'incredibly volatile' with 'extremely challenging' market conditions
findings.detail: Children's social care is forecasting £7.3m overspend, with £5.4m attributable to placements. Pressures are driven by structural deficit (additional demand), non-deliverable savings, and rising average placement costs above budgeted levels. The council explicitly warns placements 'will continue to remain under significant pressure as it remains extremely volatile both locally and nationally'.
findings.matters: Placements are identified as the largest single risk and most volatile line item. Market availability is beyond the council's control, and this is explicitly flagged as a live risk that could deteriorate further by year end.
findings.figures: £7.3m overspend, £5.4m placements pressure, £9.6m forecast placement overspend
findings.quote: Placements is the biggest single risk and is incredibly volatile. The Trust continues to mitigate and negotiate to secure placements at a lower cost. However, the market and availability of placements remains extremely challenging.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26
findings.headline: Adults social care structural deficit of £3.6m from new clients identified post-budget setting
findings.detail: Adult social care is demand-led and cannot refuse eligible clients. The £10.4m total overspend includes £3.6m arising from additional clients requiring care after the February 2025 budget was approved. Additionally, £1.8m of legacy savings targets from prior years remain formally assessed as undeliverable in 2025-26, now moved to burden 2026-27 budget planning.
findings.matters: Demand-led overspends cannot be controlled by spending discipline; they reflect statutory obligations the council must meet. Legacy undeliverable savings indicate prior-year optimism and tighter financial planning going forward.
findings.figures: £3.6m structural deficit, £10.4m total overspend, £1.8m legacy undeliverable savings
findings.quote: This includes a £3.6m structural deficit arising from additional clients requiring care after the 2025-26 budget was set

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26
findings.headline: £32.1m high needs education overspend with 70% EHCP growth against 7.5% funding uplift
findings.detail: WNC has seen 70% growth in Education Health and Care Plans since vesting, but government funding increased only 7.5%. The council remains in the bottom quartile nationally for high needs funding per pupil. This £32.1m overspend reflects a structural gap between statutory obligations (EHCPs must be funded) and government allocation. The NAO reports local authorities nationally are expected to accumulate £5bn SEND deficit by March 2026.
findings.matters: This is a statutory obligation that cannot be refused or deferred, yet funding is structural and unfunded. It signals a permanent budget pressure and questions the sustainability of the authority's financial position in this area.
findings.figures: £32.1m overspend, 70% EHCP growth, 7.5% funding increase, bottom quartile nationally, £5bn national SEND deficit
findings.quote: The forecast overspend on the high needs block totals £32.1m.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix B
findings.headline: Multiple income-based proposals (parking, planning fees, leisure) carry Amber or Red delivery risk
findings.detail: The council is seeking £3.5m+ from income generation (parking charges, planning fee increases, event income, leisure activities, facilities rentals). Across these proposals, Amber and Red ratings significantly outnumber Blue. For example: parking £142k proposed with £72k at risk; planning fee increase £250k with all £250k Amber; parking enforcement £22k with all Amber.
findings.matters: Income-based savings are volatile and reversible if uptake is lower than forecast or services are challenged. Relying on multiple unconfirmed income proposals for 14% of the savings program creates execution risk.
findings.figures: Parking regulations and charges: £84k across three schemes; Planning fees: £330k total with £310k+ Amber/Red; Event income: £96k with £96k Amber/Red
findings.quote: Introduction of car parking charges at Claret Car Park (50) 0 0 (50) 0 ... Proposed increase in fee against Householder Planning Applications (250) 0 0 (250) 0

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix B
findings.headline: Home to School Transport saving of £550k is 91% unconfirmed; £500k rated Amber and £50k Red
findings.detail: A £550k saving in Home to School Transport is proposed through 'Implementation of a number of policy and operational measures', but only £50k has any Green rating. £500k is Amber (at risk) and £50k Red (unlikely). This is a statutory or near-statutory service with significant delivery uncertainty.
findings.matters: Unconfirmed large savings in statutory services suggest either unimplemented policy changes (facing delivery or political barriers) or the council's own uncertainty about achievability. Either signals budget risk.
findings.figures: £550k total; Blue £0k; Amber £500k; Red £50k
findings.quote: Implementation of a number of policy and operational measures to deliver efficiency savings (550) 0 0 (500) (50)

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix B
findings.headline: Largest single saving—£3m Adult Social Care healthcare funding—is 83% unconfirmed and vaguely defined
findings.detail: The highest-value proposal is a £3m reduction in Adult Social Care Continued Healthcare Funding, yet only £506k is Blue (confirmed), with £2.494m Amber (at risk). The saving relies on 'Ensuring Adult Social care clients are receiving appropriate levels of funding and processes are robustly followed'—no specific delivery mechanism is stated.
findings.matters: Adult Social Care is demand-led and cost-volatile. A £3m saving that is 83% unconfirmed in the council's largest people service represents acute financial vulnerability if demand increases.
findings.figures: £3,000k total; Blue £506k; Amber £2,494k
findings.quote: Ensuring Adult Social care clients are receiving appropriate levels of funding and processes are robustly followed (3,000) (506) 0 (2,494) 0

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix B
findings.headline: Only £7m of £24.6m required savings are confirmed delivered; 72% remain unconfirmed or at risk
findings.detail: The council's 2025-26 budget depends on £24.604m in total savings. Of this, only £6.995m is Blue (Delivered and Confirmed), £11.063m is Green (likely), but £5.554m is Amber (at risk) and £991k is Red (unlikely to be achieved). This means nearly three-quarters of the required savings are not yet certain.
findings.matters: A council unable to deliver its planned savings will run an operating deficit. For a lender, this degree of unconfirmed savings indicates potential financial stress, emergency action, or reserve drawdown.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation pressures described as ongoing despite multiple mitigation work streams
findings.detail: Housing subsidy loss pressure of £176k, empty homes scheme rental income loss of £120k, and various temporary accommodation variances are partially offset by underspends, but the document explicitly notes 'Multiple work streams are in progress within the Housing service to address the Temporary Accommodation issues to mitigate future budget pressures', indicating the issue is acknowledged as structural and unresolved.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation is a statutory duty with volatile costs; work streams 'in progress' suggests solutions are not yet implemented, so pressures will likely persist into next year.
findings.figures: £176k subsidy loss + £120k empty homes income loss; net directorate position £573k overspend after offsets
findings.quote: Multiple work streams are in progress within the Housing service to address the Temporary Accommodation issues to mitigate future budget pressures.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: General contingency of £11.384m released to balance budget, consuming over half of identified overspends
findings.detail: The council identified total overspends of £20.976m across all directorates at Period 4, but required a £11.384m release from general contingency to bring the forecast outturn to £9.592m. At the halfway point of the financial year, this represents substantial contingency depletion with five months remaining.
findings.matters: Using contingency at this scale and pace leaves minimal buffer for further in-year pressures; limited flexibility to absorb unexpected costs or demand spikes in the second half of the year.
findings.figures: £20.976m identified overspends; £11.384m contingency release; £9.592m forecast outturn after contingency
findings.quote: Total WNC: 20,976; General Contingency release (11,384); Overall Net Outturn 2025-26 9,592

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Children's Trust contract overspend of £7.125m creates second-largest directorate pressure
findings.detail: The Children's Trust shows a forecast contract sum overspend of £7.125m, plus an estimate of £150k adverse movement from provisional to final outturn on the prior year, totalling £7.275m. This is the largest overspend outside adult social care and appears to be driven by contract cost pressures rather than underfunding assumptions.
findings.matters: A £7.125m mid-year contract variance suggests either poor contract forecasting at budget-setting or emerging cost pressures in children's services that will recur next year.
findings.figures: £7.125m contract sum overspend + £150k prior year adjustment
findings.quote: 2025-26 forecast contract sum overspend 7,125

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Planned NHS savings target for 2023-24 is explicitly undeliverable, alongside unmet restructure savings from 2024-25
findings.detail: The document explicitly labels an NHS savings target of £500k as 'Undeliverable NHS savings target set in 2023-24', and a further £499k restructure target from 2024-25 is similarly unmet. Together these represent nearly £1m of assumed savings that the council has already confirmed will not materialise.
findings.matters: When councils publicly mark savings as undeliverable midway through the year, it indicates either poor planning assumptions or structural issues that prevent delivery; it also suggests the council is not aligned with NHS partners on controlling joint costs.
findings.figures: £500k undeliverable NHS target + £499k unmet restructure target = £999k
findings.quote: Undeliverable NHS savings target set in 2023-24 500; Restructure and Reorganisation savings target set 2024-25 499

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix A
findings.headline: Adult social care overspend of £10.362m driven by independent care placements demand exceeding forecast by £7.677m
findings.detail: The largest single pressure across all directorates is independent care placements at £7.677m, accounting for over half the adult social care overspend. Additional pressures include staffing (£810k), client transport (£500k), and shortfalls in Better Care Fund base budgets (£358k). These are only partially offset by higher-than-expected client contributions (£1.445m).
findings.matters: Adult social care is typically a council's hardest cost to control and fastest-growing pressure; a £10.362m directorate overspend halfway through the year signals structural affordability constraints that will persist.
findings.figures: £10.362m net overspend; £7.677m independent care placements; £810k staffing; £500k client transport
findings.quote: Independent Care Placements forecast pressure 7,677

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix C
findings.headline: Investment income is below budget despite outperforming market rates
findings.detail: The council achieved 4.44% yield on 3-month investments (19 basis points above SONIA) but receivable investment income remains below the £7.69m budget assumption because cash balances available for investment were lower than anticipated (average £93m vs budgeted £144m).
findings.matters: This shows the council cannot achieve its treasury income budget due to lower than expected cash balances. Combined with the borrowing and cash flow issues described above, this indicates the council is cash-constrained and cannot carry the working balances it planned for.
findings.figures: Average treasury investments £93m (budgeted £144m); Council yield 4.44% vs SONIA 4.25%; Interest receivable forecast £7.36m (budget £7.69m)
findings.quote: The Council has exceeded the budget assumption in terms of yield. However, receivable investment income is below expectations due to lower than anticipated cash balances available for investment.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix C
findings.headline: Treasury budget is £1m under pressure from cash flow timing complexity
findings.detail: The council is forecasting a £1m variance (net finance costs £9.54m vs budget £8.54m). The council acknowledges that cash flow timing between investment and borrowing activity is creating short-term pressures that differ from budget assumptions, and these are being monitored.
findings.matters: A budget pressure specifically attributed to short-term cash flow timing risk shows the council struggled to forecast its cash position accurately and is now managing ad-hoc shortfalls. This is a warning sign for treasury control.
findings.figures: £1.00m forecast variance on net finance costs (budget £8.54m, forecast £9.54m); Financing costs up £0.67m (£16.23m to £16.90m); Interest receivable down £0.33m (£7.69m to £7.36m)
findings.quote: Ongoing budget monitoring has highlighted a risk of short-term cash flow pressures due to the timing of investment and borrowing activity. This reflects the complexity of balancing capital financing, operational needs, and available cash resources within the financial year, as compared to assumed levels.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix C
findings.headline: Large working capital surplus of £213m creates cash management complexity and risk
findings.detail: The council holds £213m in working capital that must be carefully managed for liquidity and operational needs. This is a substantial balance that complicates cash forecasting and indicates either over-collection of income or deferred spending.
findings.matters: A very large cash surplus alongside cash flow timing pressures (see theme below) suggests poor cash forecasting or structural mismatch between income timing and spend timing. A lender will question whether the council truly understands its cash position.
findings.figures: £213m working capital surplus
findings.quote: A working capital surplus of £213m, which, while positive, must be carefully managed to ensure liquidity and meet operational needs.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix C
findings.headline: Borrowing strategy revised and accelerated mid-year to secure liquidity
findings.detail: The council brought forward borrowing in-year as part of a reassessed strategy. This appears reactive to service demand pressures and the cash position revealed by year-end accounts, and was necessary to maintain sufficient liquidity for the capital programme.
findings.matters: Mid-year revision of borrowing strategy signals the council's original plan became unaffordable or unworkable, and it had to act to avoid cash flow difficulty. This is a material change of direction.
findings.figures: £107m borrowing raised in period (£10m PWLB HRA, £97m temporary from other authorities)
findings.quote: These factors, alongside sustained service demand pressures, have prompted a reassessment of the timing and scale of planned borrowing. Some borrowing has been brought forward in-year to maintain sufficient liquidity and ensure continuity of the capital programme.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Monitoring Period 4 - Financial Year 2025-26 - Appendix C
findings.headline: Council has depleted internal reserves and remains severely under-borrowed by £313m
findings.detail: The audited accounts confirm an under-borrowed position of £313m (gap between capital financing requirement and actual borrowing) and prior use of £100m of internal reserves to support capital investment. This has reduced the scope for further internal borrowing and forced the council to externalize borrowing.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether the council can fund future capital programmes. A £313m under-borrowed position combined with £100m already drawn from reserves means the council has limited internal liquidity cushion remaining and will depend on external borrowing.
findings.figures: £313m under-borrowed position; £100m previous internal reserve draw; £107m borrowed in period; £743m current loan portfolio
findings.quote: An under-borrowed position of £313m, indicating a gap between the capital financing requirement and actual borrowing. Previous use of £100m of internal reserves to support capital investment, reducing the scope for further internal borrowing.
